# pikopod

> pikopod is an open-source sandbox for the third-party APIs you depend on. Built from the provider's spec, it fails on purpose: rehearsal scenarios run against a deterministic sandbox before you ship, and when production fails anyway, the incident replays into the same sandbox so you fix it on a laptop and keep the fix as a test.

pikopod is a command-line tool written in Go. It builds an offline sandbox from a provider's OpenAPI spec or docs URL, wraps webhooks, and runs failure-rehearsal scenarios (declines, timeouts, retry storms, duplicate deliveries) that a real provider never lets you practice on. `pikopod spec-diff --fail-on` gates CI when a provider's spec drifts, and `pikopod agent replay --ci` turns a captured production incident into a regression gate on every build. Licensed under Apache-2.0.

## Docs

- [Install](https://github.com/pikopod/pikopod#install): `go install github.com/pikopod/pikopod/cmd/pikopod@latest` and the try-it-in-ten-seconds quickstart.
- [Sandbox overview](https://docs.pikopod.com/sandbox/overview): the deterministic sandbox built from the provider's spec.
- [Scenarios overview](https://docs.pikopod.com/scenarios/overview): writing failure-rehearsal scenarios, standing state, and binding to real endpoints.
- [Spec diff](https://docs.pikopod.com/gate/spec-diff): gating CI when a provider's spec drifts.
- [Reproduce](https://docs.pikopod.com/reproduce/reproduce): turning a production incident fingerprint into a committed scenario.
- [Drift](https://docs.pikopod.com/observe/drift) and [Replay gate](https://docs.pikopod.com/observe/replay-gate): replaying recorded production traffic against every build.
